outcome: Accelerated nodes, model serving and a document retrieval layer arrive as one engineered platform, keeping every prompt and response inside the organisation.
overview: Organisations that cannot send their documents to a hosted model service, and do not want to assemble an accelerator platform from parts, are the audience for this record. GPT-in-a-Box packages accelerated nodes, model serving and the surrounding platform as one engineered configuration on infrastructure the organisation owns. What it does not package is the part that decides whether the investment pays: a use case with a named owner, data that is actually available, and a way to tell whether the output is good enough.

benefits.text: Model inference runs entirely inside the organisation’s own infrastructure
benefits.limits: Residency is a property of the deployment and says nothing about the licensing of the models or data used on it

benefits.text: Accelerators, serving and platform arrive as an engineered configuration rather than as parts
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance rather than from host counts or invoice history; a design built on the latter is a quotation with an architecture attached

benefits.text: The platform runs alongside the existing estate under one operating model
benefits.limits: Operating the platform is not the same as operating a model lifecycle; the second is a discipline the organisation still has to build

residency: Documents, prompts, responses and model weights all remain on organisation-owned infrastructure

notFor.situation: An organisation permitted to use a hosted model service for the data in question
notFor.why: On-premises accelerated infrastructure carries capital and operating cost a hosted service does not

notFor.situation: An organisation with no defined use case and no evaluation method
notFor.why: Infrastructure sized against an undefined use case is a capital commitment against an assumption

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with accredited Nutanix and NVIDIA implementation partners · Duration: 12–16 weeks to a first use case in production, accelerator lead time excluded
Support model: Vendor hardware and software support; Redington coordinates the vendor cases across both.
1) Define — use case, owner, evaluation method, document availability and facility check
2) Design — node sizing, serving layout and retrieval design
3) Build — platform installed, models served, retrieval layer connected
4) Deliver and hand over — first use case in production against its evaluation method, operations handed over
deliverables: Prompts, documents and responses demonstrably do not leave the organisation’s network
The first use case is evaluated against its agreed method rather than demonstrated
A second use case can be onboarded by the customer team using the documented path
effort: 12–16 weeks to a first use case in production, accelerator lead time excluded
